text:
asha: heads-up — pulled the last 30d KMS grant audit and there are a handful of service principals with recent admin-grant events but no owner recorded. looks like delegation drift.
liam: can you paste the query? happy to run a quick owner backfill.
asha: sure — ran this against our audit index:
```
SELECT principal, grant_type, resource, timestamp FROM kms_audit
WHERE grant_type = 'ADMIN' AND timestamp > now()-30d
ORDER BY timestamp desc
LIMIT 50;
```
asha: top offenders: svc-eval-runner, svc-data-sync, svc-legacy-ingest. svc-legacy-ingest had a grant yesterday at 04:12 UTC.
matt: ugh svc-legacy-ingest — that's the one we deprecated but kept for a snapshot job. who owns that snapshot job now?
anya: cc @matt I think infra took it over during the migration. matt can you confirm ownership and whether we still need admin on KMS for it?
matt: confirming — infra owns it, but they only need decrypt access, not admin. looks like an accidental promote from an older script.
oncall-sre: security-bot also flagged an access anomaly for svc-eval-runner 2 days ago with an unusual IP range. logging the incident ID: INC-2026-789.
security-bot: ALERT INC-2026-789: anomalous KMS admin grant observed for principal svc-eval-runner — intensity=medium. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-789
asha: proposal: run a short audit + temporary rollback window. plan:
1) list all principals with admin grants in last 30d
2) email owners (or tag teams) to justify admin within 48h
3) auto-revoke admin if no justification after 72h
4) if revoke impacts jobs, provide a 2-hour emergency re-elevate playbook
liam: +1. can we avoid noisy emails? maybe just DM owners first and only pager if critical (like production decryption failures).
anya: fine by me. suggest also create a small canary that attempts decrypt for known jobs to catch false positives before mass revoke.
matt: I can own the canary and run it in a staging namespace.
oncall-sre: will add monitoring alerts for failed decrypts tied to the canary and prod jobs. low false-positive tolerance.
asha: thanks. i'll assemble the owner list and push a short Slack DM template. DM template draft:
"Hey <owner>, we detected an ADMIN KMS grant for <principal>. Please confirm whether admin access is required and provide justification or request a scoped role by <deadline>. If no response, we'll auto-revoke on <date>." 
liam: nit — add how to request scoped role and link to the self-serve form: https://redwood.internal/sec/access-requests
asha: good call. i'll include that.
matt: timeline ok — i'll run the canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC and report.
anya: i'll prepare the canary runbook and post it in #eng-ops after it's ready.
security-bot: NOTE: scheduled task: access-review-batch-4911223344 queued (eta 24h). 
asha: assigning ownership: asa -> owner outreach, liam -> DM automation + audit query, matt -> canary and rollback playbook, oncall-sre -> monitor + incident link. i'll update the runbook and mark the task in the audit tracker.
liam: I'll drop a short script for owner extraction + DM automation. snippet:
```
for p in $(cat principals.txt); do
  owner=$(lookup_owner $p)
  send_dm $owner "Found ADMIN grant for $p — please respond"
done
```
oncall-sre: flagged in pager duty: assigned to infra on rotation if revoke triggers job failure.
asha: cool. will kick this off in the morning. if anyone sees additional principals not in my list ping me here.
matt: thx. will confirm infra ownership for svc-legacy-ingest by EOD.
anya: FYI — adding a short postmortem template to document any accidental revokes so we can improve automation.
asha: excellent. closing the loop here — will post updates as owners respond. :thumbsup:
